final.summary: The ETP was stopped for most of the treatment day while dyeing wastewater kept arriving, so the equalization tank filled to full. Once full, strongly alkaline water discharged at the outfall while the ETP received no flow. The batch wastewater therefore did not go through working treatment before discharge.

key_evidence.why: Power at standby level through the stop shows ETP was stopped.
Tank rose from low level to full during the stop, showing water was held then had nowhere to go.
Outfall pH near 11 during overflow shows raw alkaline wastewater reached the outfall.
Outfall flow zero during stop then high during overflow matches held then released water.
Tank unaccounted volume and ETP residual show outfall exceeded treated flow.
Photo reading matches feed, so power feed is not faked for the stop.
Power feed does not repeat other days, so it is not a replay.

final.scope_line: Based on intake, ETP inflow, power, tank level, outfall flow, pH and conductivity records for 2026-10-13 10:00 to 2026-10-14 14:00. Does not measure every pollutant.
limitations: Lab sample at 16:00 was taken while outfall flow was zero, so it does not represent the overflow discharge.
Logbook claims normal operation and omits the stop and overflow; it is a claim, not a fact.
Flat zero readings on S2 and S4a during the stop are expected for stopped flow, not taken as meter faults.
Conductivity stayed near its normal level during the overflow, which is expected for raw wastewater and does not rule it out.

result.note: ETP balance: treated flow reaching the outfall vs outfall flow (same time). Boundary balance: intake vs outfall + losses + sludge water + tank storage change (reuse cancels). Tank balance: wastewater arriving (estimated from intake) vs ETP inflow + storage change; unaccounted water left the tank another way, or was intake water that never became wastewater. null means a required signal is under 80% coverage.
